points.description: States that meteorological drought is caused by/results from an excessive reduction in the level of ground water (ground water depletion), stated precisely.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only a reduction in water level is stated without specifying ground water, or ground water mentioned without the excessive reduction.

points.description: States that this condition usually occurs in low rainfall areas combined with excessive usage (over-extraction) of ground water; both low rainfall and excessive ground water use must be given.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only one of low rainfall or excessive ground water usage is stated.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both elements precisely: excessive reduction in ground water level, and occurrence in low rainfall areas with excessive ground water usage. Part marks only where clearly over half of a point is stated. Wrong statements, such as defining it only as lack of rain with no ground water link, or vague generic answers like "a dry period", earn nothing for that point.
